title: Intent Analysis
description: Output contract of SEARCH-INTENT.md (module 01, PLAN phase). One object per target query: the classified search intent, the five analysis dimensions (user goal, main question, expected content format, journey stage, important subtopics), the structure recommendation, and data availability. Data Availability Policy: data_availability.serp_data MUST be true only when real SERP results were actually provided; never invent SERP observations, and let missing SERP data lower intent_confidence rather than being papered over.

query.description: The target query this analysis classifies, verbatim.

primary_intent.description: The dominant intent. Exactly one. Transactional and navigational outcomes are flagged via structure_recommendation rather than silently turned into articles.

intent_confidence.description: Honesty about the classification basis. No SERP data caps confidence at medium unless the query pattern is decisive (SEARCH-INTENT.md rule SEO-SI-10).

mixed_intent.description: True when the query or the real SERP suggests more than one intent; the dominant intent is served, the secondary is acknowledged.

secondary_intent.description: The non-dominant intent when mixed_intent is true; MUST be null otherwise.

user_goal.description: What the user is ultimately trying to accomplish, phrased from the user's perspective.

main_question.description: The single question the article must answer, phrased as the user would state it. Drives validation check SEO-V02.

expected_format.description: Content format(s) the intent implies and, when real SERP data exists, the formats the live results reward.

journey_stage.description: The searcher's journey stage; calibrates depth and tone.

important_subtopics.description: Subtopics a fully satisfied reader expects to find; becomes required-subtopic material for TOPIC-COVERAGE.md.

recommended_archetype.description: The archetype the intent demands per the structure-must-match-intent mapping. product_landing and brand_page are flags: the CMS usually should not create an article for that intent.

rationale.description: One to three sentences of justification, including any SERP confirmation, confidence cap, or intent flip.

serp_data.description: True only when real SERP results were actually provided. Never true for imagined results.

notes.description: What was and was not available, and how confidence was affected.
